newsitem.title: USA: Thunderstorms down lines, cut power in Houston.
newsitem.headline: Thunderstorms down lines, cut power in Houston.

text.p: A fast-moving line of tornadic thunderstorms left an estimated 152,000 customers without power on Tuesday as it moved through the Houston area, a spokesman with Houston Lighting and Power Co said.

That total was expected to rise in the wake of a storm that spawned at least three tornadic funnel clouds as it moved through Harris County tracking southeast toward the Gulf coast, utility and emergency officials said.
"We have 152,000 customers without power right now, but that number's probably going to go up," utility spokesman Graham Painter said.
Emergency officials said three tornadoes were sighted in the area, and strong winds ripped down tree limbs and broke out glass in some downtown buildings.
There were no immediate reports of injuries and minimal damage was reported. Officials did not expect significant flooding in the area as tornado warnings were lifted in Harris County.
A severe thunderstorm warning remained in place for coastal Texas counties southeast of Houston into the afternoon.
Crews from HL&P, a unit of Houston Industries, were repairing downed power lines and blown transformers to restore power, Painter said.
